title: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
pitch: A bounty hunter retires escaped androids in a ruined San Francisco, and starts to doubt what separates them from humans. The basis for Blade Runner.

chapters.g: After a world war most animals are gone, and owning a real animal is a mark of status and care.
Androids are detected with an empathy test, the only sure difference from humans.
Deckard must retire six escaped Nexus-6 androids in a single long day.
Androids that seem human, and humans who seem cold, blur the line.
A shared empathy religion that may be fake, and still matters.

ideas: Empathy may be what makes us human.
Tests for being human can fail.
Machines that seem human raise moral questions.
Real and fake may matter less than how we treat others.

args.a: The novel shows a test for machine minds can never be complete.
args.c: Some read the androids as simply lacking empathy, so the line holds.

args.a: We may owe moral care to beings that seem human.
args.c: Others argue appearance is not enough to deserve rights.

questions: Would you pass the Voigt-Kampff test?
What test would you use to tell an AI from a person?
Does it matter if the empathy you feel is for something fake?

quiz.q: What film is based on the novel?
What is a status symbol on this Earth?
